title: `merge --ready` runs the records step and pushes it before it marks a PR ready, so a ready PR never carries a stale records page
why:
Coordinator 05:47 CST Nov 15 (relayed; triage read no PR or log). Lane ready-refreshes-records (session_013NEJL2x8RHNnMo2B3gWMxy, sonnet, guard or check: yes) started on the consultant's order of 05:46 CST: consultant's pick under the owner's 20:18 CST Nov 14 words, not an owner-typed pick. Fix: `merge --ready` runs the records step and pushes it before it marks a PR ready. Cost it stops (coordinator's relay): the merge tool refused ready PRs #3255 and #3472 tonight for a stale records page, each costing a full extra CI run. The lane also hunts any other refusal that only shows after the ready run. The lane is told to report whether any record names an owner of `merge.readyChecks` (triage's 04:30 CST read found none; see step ready-check-names-tree). Kin steps (all exist, checked 05:46 CST): records-page-before-ready (doing, older lane; the same class, and its ruling own-830-c-ci-scope-green-before-head kept the refusal at merge and the ready records push), records-stale-refuses-on-ready (done), ready-push-merges-main (doing), ready-pr-touched-tests, ready-check-names-tree. Not an alias of records-page-before-ready: that step's open fix is rebuilding before the ready run in general; this lane's fix is the `--ready` push alone. Overlap is the lane's first read. FINDING 05:49 CST Nov 15 (lane's report, relayed 05:48 CST; triage read none of the PRs or logs): the refusals on #3255 and #3472 came after runner 10 marked ready by MCP, not by `merge N --ready`, so the records step never ran; the tool did what decision records-index-at-merge says (lane's read of draft_step, merge/merge.py:4114; runner 10's refusal lines relayed by the coordinator). Triage's read of the decision on main (GitHub, 05:49 CST): it says 'the batch runner marks the PR ready by its session's route (route pr-ready-mcp-cloud), after the draft run of the pushed head shows' (the sentence runs from line 16 to 17 in the stable copy). Skill ci-hygiene line 69 says the ready route is `merge <pr> --ready`, which runs the records step. The two texts clash (confirmed by triage's read; the MCP-ready bypass itself is the lane's read). Lane options: (a) record-only: rewrite that decision sentence to say the runner readies with `merge N --ready` (lane's recommendation, not the owner's); (b) a guard refusing MCP update_pull_request draft=false on a PR with no --ready run (risk: false alarms in cloud where --ready's own mark may be refused by GraphQL); (c) confirm heals the page (restarts CI; against the decision). Lane builds nothing; says (a) to its parent. Undoable and record-only, so no owner item; coordinator/consultant decide. PICK 05:50 CST Nov 15 (coordinator's pick, undoable, relayed; not the owner's): option (a) is the picked route. The lane rewrites decision records-index-at-merge (the sentence on the runner marking ready by MCP route) in place so the runner readies with `merge N --ready`, and aligns skill ci-hygiene line 69. Not (b): no second incident yet and a cloud false-alarm risk; (b) is filed as later low step ready-mcp-mark-guard. The lane's PR is a draft and gets a fresh reviewer read, since a rule's text changes. Runner 10 was asked to try `merge N --ready` on #3255 and #3496 and report any refusal.

SIGHTING 06:05 CST Nov 15 (coordinator, relayed; triage read no log): #3472's first ready mark ended in the records refusal; its second ready mark (05:46) then passed, with the records commit 2f09c768b9ac pushed by the records step, and the PR merged 06:03:22 CST on green ready run 43710479473 (GitHub read). How the second mark was made (merge N --ready or MCP) was not stated.

DATA 06:06 CST Nov 15 (coordinator 06:05, from runner 10's log; relayed twice, read by neither coordinator nor triage): `merge 3255 --ready` ran in the cloud at about 06:04 CST. It merged origin/main into the branch (new head df7ff9e441d6 on lane/role-gaps-arbiter-line), ran the records step and the ready checks (all pass), then printed that #3255 stays a draft because the tool sends no GraphQL, and to mark ready by MCP update_pull_request draft=false after the draft run shows, then run `--confirm`. So the cloud sequence is `--ready` on the draft, MCP mark, `--confirm`; the two refusals tonight (#3255, #3472) came from skipping `--ready`. The coordinator told the lane to write that three-step order in both texts (decision records-index-at-merge and ci-hygiene line 69), pointing at the tool's hint.

EVIDENCE 06:55 CST Nov 15 (coordinator 06:55, relayed; triage read no log): #3255 is the first merge by the cloud order. Runner 10 ran `merge --ready` (main merge and records step), marked ready by MCP at 06:10, and merged it alone on green ready run 43712398831 at head df7ff9e441d6 (the coordinator names no refusal on this path; that absence is not a read of runner 10's log). GitHub read by triage at 06:55 CST: closed, merged true, merged_at 06:53:35 CST, run 43712398831 concluded success. One merge is a single sighting, not a proof.
